s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive neurological deficit with a history of malignancy
salient_findings: 30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe
History of breast cancer with metastasis
key_facts: 46-year-old Japanese woman
History of epilepsy
Redness and swelling of the right breast
Erythema and swelling in the lower right breast
54 × 41 × 31 mm low-echo mass with partially unclear margins in the outer right breast
Invasive ductal carcinoma, high grade, ER+, PgR–, HER2 3+, Ki67 70%
Increased uptake in the right axilla, anterior mediastinum, left pleura, and liver on whole-body PET-CT
Received four cycles of FEC chemotherapy
Received trastuzumab plus pertuzumab with docetaxel
Achieved a clinical complete response maintained for 23 months
Developed a persistent headache two years after treatment initiation
30-mm mass lesion in the right temporal lobe on CT and MRI of the head

shortlist.label: Brain metastasis from breast cancer
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer with high-grade features and HER2 positivity, now presenting with a mass lesion in the brain

shortlist.label: Glioblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: New onset of persistent headache and a mass lesion in the temporal lobe, a common location for glioblastoma

shortlist.label: Breast cancer leptomeningeal metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: History of breast cancer with stage IV disease and now presenting with neurological symptoms and a mass lesion in the brain

shortlist.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass lesion in the brain and a history of immunosuppression due to chemotherapy

shortlist.label: Cerebral metastasis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple metastatic sites identified in the past, including liver and lymph nodes, increasing the likelihood of cerebral involvement

raw.rationale: The patient has a history of stage IV breast cancer with a clinical complete response to treatment, and now presents with a mass lesion in the right temporal lobe, which is consistent with metastasis to the brain from the primary breast cancer.

rejected.label: Glioblastoma
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest a primary brain tumor, and the patient's history of breast cancer makes metastasis more likely.

rejected.label: Breast cancer leptomeningeal metastasis
rejected.why: The mass lesion is localized to the right temporal lobe, rather than being diffuse or involving the leptomeninges.

rejected.label: Primary central nervous system lymphoma
rejected.why: There is no evidence to suggest a lymphoma, and the patient's history of breast cancer makes metastasis more likely.

rejected.label: Cerebral metastasis
rejected.why: This option is too broad, as the patient's history and presentation suggest metastasis from the breast cancer specifically, rather than an unspecified primary tumor.
